description.narrative: Livability and climate resilience in selected cities in priority industrial corridors enhanced.

At least 28,498 tons of carbon dioxide equivalent per year in greenhouse gas emissions avoided (2019 baseline: 0). Progress/Status: Target year is 2026 - but on track to achieve the target. Data Source: Program quarterly progress reports. Actual value:

At least 3,000 cubic meters/day of treated wastewater reused for industrial purposes in at least one city (Ambur) (2019 baseline: 0). Progress/Status: Target year is 2026 - but on track to achieve the target. Data Source: Program quarterly progress reports. Actual value:

Collection and treatment of sewage in project coverage areas of four cities increased to 100% of householdsd (2019 baseline: sewage collected from 0% of households in coverage areas). Progress/Status: Target year is 2026 - but on track to achieve the target. Data Source: Program quarterly progress reports. Actual value:

Nonrevenue water in coverage areas in two cities (Madurai and Tiruppur) reduced to 20%. Progress/Status: Target year is 2026 - but on track to achieve the target. Data Source: Program quarterly progress reports. Actual value:

Frequency and duration of piped water supply improved to at least 6 hours/day provided to 100% of households in project coverage area in two cities (Madurai and Tiruppur) (2019 baseline: 65.8% in Madurai and 61.4% in Tiruppur with water for 1 hour/day or less, 22.5% in Madurai and 38.4% in Tiruppur with water for 4 hours/day or less, 57% of households in Madurai and 73% in Tiruppur connected to piped water). Progress/Status: Target year is 2026 - but on track to achieve the target. Data Source: Program quarterly progress reports. Actual value:

Collection efficiency of water supply user fees in project areas in Madurai increased to 90% and in Tiruppur maintained at 90% (2019 baseline: Madurai, 76%; Tiruppur, 90%) and collection efficiency of sewerage user fees in project areas increased in Ambur to 67%, in Tiruchirappalli to 81%, in Tiruppur to 90%, and in Vellore to 66% (2019 baseline: 0% in Ambur, Tiruchirappalli, Tiruppur, and Vellore). Progress/Status: Target year is 2026 - but on track to achieve the target. Data Source: Program quarterly progress reports. Actual value:
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Climate-resilient sewage collection and treatment, and drainage systems developed in four cities (Ambur, Tiruchirappalli, Tiruppur, and Vellore) Indicator: A total of 1,328 km of new sewage collection pipelines commissioned and connected to 152,593 households in four ULBs (Ambur, Tiruchirappalli, Tiruppur, and Vellore) including 100% poor and women-headed households in the coverage area (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Contracts awarded and current progress is below: Ambur 1 - 100 % Tiruppur 1 - 100 % Tiruppur 2 - 100 % Tiruppur 3 - 100 % Tiruchirappalli - 99% Vellore - 100%
1179.23 km (as per present site condition 1183.62 km) of new sewerage collection pipelines laid & 140320 HSCs provided (as per present site condition 140342 Nos).​
As of June 2025, under Tranche 02, a total of 1,59,594 households were covered under the Underground Sewerage Scheme (UGSS) component across four ULBs—Ambur, Vellore, Tiruchirappalli, and Tiruppur—as per the DPR/revised estimates approved by DMA. ​
Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Climate-resilient sewage collection and treatment, and drainage systems developed in four cities (Ambur, Tiruchirappalli, Tiruppur, and Vellore) Indicator: A total of 25 sewage pump stations and 44 lift stations in four ULBs (Ambur, Tiruchirappalli, Tiruppur, and Vellore) with capacity of 3,690 kilowatts added (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Contracts awarded and current progress is below: Tiruppur 1 - physically completed Tiruppur 2 - physically completed Tiruppur 3 - physically completed Ambur - physically completed Vellore - 91%
Works are in progress in various stages at 19 sewage pump stations and 99 lift stations. Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Climate-resilient sewage collection and treatment, and drainage systems developed in four cities (Ambur, Tiruchirappalli, Tiruppur, and Vellore) Indicator: Eight (two per city in four ULBs: Ambur, Tiruchirappalli, Tiruppur, and Vellore) all-female community-based water and sanitation committees formed and improved knowledge of benefits of household connection to sewage collection system reported by at least 80% of trained members (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Total10 all-female WSCs have been formed in Ambur (2),Vellore (2) Trichy (2), Madurai (2) and Tiruppur (2) in T2 ULBs. ​
Training on household connection of sewage collection system was conducted for 60 members in 6 WSCs at 3 ULBs. The improved knowledge of benefits of household connection to sewage collection system was reported by 90% of the trained members.​ Data Source: Pre-and post-training surveys Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance in ten cities strengthened Indicator: By 2025, 300 students, teachers, and administrators (at least 50% women); and improved awareness on water conservation and hygiene reported by at least 50% of members of 12 women groups in three cities (Ambur, Madurai and Tiruppur) (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Target Achieved​
A total of 5 awareness programs were conducted in 5 ULBs (Tiruppur: 165; Madurai: 382; Vellore: 196; Ambur: 127; Tiruchirappalli: 121) till March 2023, reaching 991 students, teachers, and administrators, of which 692 (70%) were females. ​
Additionally, 5 awareness programs were conducted for SHG members in the same 5 ULBs, with a total of 226 women participants. Data Source: Pre- and post-awareness campaign sample survey Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance in ten cities strengthened Indicator: By 2025, agreements with industry for treated wastewater reuse signed by at least four cities under the performance-based grant (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: GIAC consultants have been mobilized and they have initiated necessary steps to support the CMA in complying with the target indicator. Data Source: Project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance in ten cities strengthened Indicator: By 2025, fecal sludge management, in areas not covered by centralized sewerage systems, implemented by at least five cities under the performance-based grant (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: GIAC consultants have been mobilized and they have initiated necessary steps to support the CMA in complying with the target indicator. Data Source: Project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance in ten cities strengthened Indicator: By 2025, improved knowledge on approaches to integrating gender in urban governance, implementing gender action plans, and monitoring and reporting on gender equality results, reported by 30 ULB staff (including at least 80% of eligible women staff) for three project cities (Ambur, Madurai, and Tiruppur) (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Conducted 3 training programs on POSH ACT 2013 for 3 ULBs staffs (both male & female) covering 160 out of which 102 (64%) were females. (Including DMA staffs in Chennai)​
Finalization of Bi-lingual module to be rolled out.​
Training module on Gender mainstreaming in urban planning and infrastructure - target group mix of CMA & ULB officials as per the GAP Target.​
Training module on Gender Action Planning and Monitoring for mainstreaming gender in urban governance - target group mix of CMA & ULB officials as per the GAP Target. Data Source: Project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Water supply systems in two cities (Madurai and Tiruppur) improved with smart features Indicator: A total of 1,260 km new water distribution pipelines commissioned within 66 new district metered areas and metered connections provided to 188,900 households in Tiruppur and Madurai (100% households including poor and women-headed households in coverage area) (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: The contracts are awarded, and current progress is below: Tiruppur 4 - 100% Tiruppur 5 - 100% Madurai 4 - 100% Tiruppur 6 - 100%
Works are in progress and Distribution system laid for a length of 2177.79 km (as per present site condition 2182.886 km) and 172757 Nos of HSCs has been provided (as per present site condition 172543 Nos).​
In Madurai, as of June 2025, out of 1,68,417 households, 31,999 are women-owned, accounting for approx. 19% of the total households. ​
The Madurai ULB has a total of 24,420 BPL/poor households, of which 5,128 are headed by women, constituting around 21% of the BPL households. Data Source: ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Water supply systems in two cities (Madurai and Tiruppur) improved with smart features Indicator: A total of 66 new reservoirs (Tiruppur and Madurai) with combined capacity of 92 million liters constructed (2017 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: 66 new reservoirs (Tiruppur and Madurai) with combined capacity of 92 million liters constructed​. Tiruppur 4 - 99% Data Source: ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Water supply systems in two cities (Madurai and Tiruppur) improved with smart features Indicator: At least 80% technical staff from each implementing agency in two cities (Madurai and Tiruppur) reported improved knowledge and skills in nonrevenue water reduction, with 75% participation of women technical staff in trainings (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Conducted 6 training programs in 3 ULBs for 206 staffs out of which 32 (16%) were female participants. Data Source: Pre- and post-training survey Actual value:

Output: Water supply systems in two cities (Madurai and Tiruppur) improved with smart features Indicator: Three new pump stations (Tiruppur and Madurai) with combined capacity of 7,225 kilowatts installed, and 196 km of new transmission mains maximizing gravity flow in Madurai, and 230 km of feeder mains constructed (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: The contracts are awarded, and current progress is below: Tiruppur 1 - physically completed Tiruupur 3 - physically completed Madurai 1 - physically completed Madurai 3 - physically completed
3 new pumping stations constructed and 199.179 km (as per present site condition 199.179 km) of new transmission and 190.78 km (as per present site condition 191.18 km) of feeder mains has been laid. Data Source: ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Water supply systems in two cities (Madurai and Tiruppur) improved with smart features Indicator: Two new intakes and two new water treatment plants with combined capacity of 321 MLD installed in Tiruppur and Madurai (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Two new intakes and two new water treatment plants with combined capacity of 321 MLD installed in Tiruppur and Madurai
Data Source: ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Actual value:

Output: Climate-resilient sewage collection and treatment, and drainage systems developed in four cities (Ambur, Tiruchirappalli, Tiruppur, and Vellore) Indicator: One existing STP with capacity of 15 MLD rehabilitated (Tiruppur) and two new STPs (Ambur and Tiruppur) with total capacity of 72.71 MLD added Progress/Status: Contracts are awarded. The physical works have been completed for STPs in Tiruppur and Ambur both. Data Source: Periodic ULB records and project quarterly progress reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not Applicable Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: Not Applicable Target year: 2025 Target value: 1

Output: Institutional capacity, public awareness, and urban governance in ten cities strengthened Indicator: By 2023, new database on urban management for three project cities (Ambur, Madurai, and Tiruppur) established at the urban data and governance improvement cell in CMA, with sex-disaggregated data where applicable (2019 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: UDGIC cell is yet to be operational. ​
The draft design document prepared by GIAC provision for capturing sex disaggregated data has been incorporated. ​
GIAC has collected the sex disaggregated data on staffs, elected representatives and Standing Committee members from 5 ULBs. The staff data with sex disaggregated has been uploaded and published by ULBs in their websites. ​
The same has been reported and recommended to release of Performance Incentive Grant for PI5.( 2023-24). Data Source: Project quarterly progress reports Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2023 Target value: Y
